name: Fall 2026

reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: All right, so we’ve gone from starting this season’s reviews, and the first one is a terrible VRMMORPG where you can’t log out, but then you can die and it matters, but it also seems like it doesn’t matter. I don’t know if the concept is here, but the main guy appeared to be kind of a turd who was in the middle of some quest and tried to screw it over for VR… I’m not watching more of this.

So from hearing others, this is a manga that I didn’t read, but it’s like 20 years old, something like that, and it’s based around telephone cards, which were the way that everybody communicated and used very extensively in the 90s through the mid 2000s. I think they did a good job of taking it and moving it forward, making it an even weirder thing. The other thing I’m getting the vibe of is I would call it a semi-nostalgia show from the era where the manga was made, so I definitely get these big 2005 vibes from the character design, art styling, production, etc. Doesn’t hurt that Satelight is the primary anime studio doing this. So overall, I’m curious to see where the episodes go, and hopefully they picked it up as an anime project from a long forgotten manga because the manga is good, and hopefully the anime will be good too.

reviewed.titleEN: Hello, I am a Witch and my Crush Wants me to Make a Love Potion!
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Well, this title already has me terrified. Production values are fine, but they did give the main character, who is the witch, the crossed bangs that are traditionally reserved for the shonen boy protagonist. I guess the best thing is that within the first five minutes they did get to the crux of the title of the show: the knight that the witch has a crush on came and asked for a love potion, and then they played the opening. Definitely just a stupid show, will not watch.

reviewed.titleEN: Reborn as a Space Mercenary: I Woke Up Piloting the Strongest Starship!
reviewed.review: So, big exhale to start this show off, based on the title. Let’s go with the positive: they took the reincarnated-into-a-VRMMORPG premise and moved it from the high fantasy setting and put it in space. Everything else about this show is terrible, but if you watch the opening and you like it, then that’s probably why that’s the opening. So this is definitely the worst show of the season… thus far.

reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: So this guy literally got divorced from his wife because she accused him of hiding things, because he likes cute stuff and couldn’t acknowledge that. And now he’s living a great life and is totally fine, but he’s still completely hiding it from everyone and himself. It makes this main character, who’s supposed to be kind of a nice, charming fuddy-duddy ojisan type, very unlikable, because he is not honest with himself and destroyed his marriage for no reason. But I’m probably overanalyzing this show, and this is definitely all the time I’m gonna spend on it.

reviewed.titleEN: Magic Repo Man: Dumped by My Party, I'll Cash In With a Cute Support Fairy to Become the Strongest!
reviewed.review: So now I’m not sure if the other show that I said was the worst of this season is the worst, or if this one is. This one is definitely the worst drawn, animated, whatever one. It’s super low budget, super low quality, super low imagination. I guess the only thing it has going for it is that it’s not an isekai.

reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: “Bad. Really bad.” That’s a quote from the main character in this show. So the premise is that the main guy gets isekai’d into an eroge (erotic/hentai game), and he’s a complete degenerate at playing them, to the point of trying to speedrun some of them and generating spreadsheets about how to speedrun through these games, particularly the one that he gets isekai’d into. How do I know this? Because the first six minutes of the show are literally all exposition. For a show that’s supposed to be about someone isekai’d into an eroge, they don’t even have an opening, or any cute girls or ridiculous scenarios within the first six minutes or so. So they’re failing at even their low standard of scenario, and even achieving that.
So I thought this might actually start out kind of cool, but then it immediately dumped into the soul transfer into another body of an aristocrat, blah blah blah, oh boy.
It's lightweight pornography. The rest of it is high fantasy something blah blah blah. It's not worth watching.

So this is some sort of show about girls in their final year of high school trying to figure out where to go to college, but something to do with travel. I really don't care; not interested. It's not the worst offensive thing, but I was also looking at the clock after three minutes wondering if the time was up yet.
Also, separately, HIDIVE has not fixed their audio stuff yet, so everything on their platform now just sounds awful, and it makes it very hard to watch shows without already thinking the production values are terrible when it's more their streaming platform.

So I made it to the first ad, which makes me say, Amazon, I don't pay you enough freaking money. It's actually kind of cool. It's very low budget, but the opening scene reminds me of the garbage truck scene from the Ghost in the Shell movie. The characters are all 3D CG, and it looks not bad. I hope they're doing it for whatever technical reasons they felt made things look and behave better. The backgrounds and stuff are all done pretty nicely, and the production value seems pretty good. The opening is pretty ridiculous. It appears there's some sort of wheelchair-bound guy who's a crazy fighter, just from seeing the opening, so I'm hopeful the show could actually be pretty fun.

reviewed.titleEN: The Seven Knights of the Marronnier Kingdom
reviewed.review: So the show is potentially more interesting than I was worried it was going to be. It appears to be less of a reverse harem show and something more along the lines of an adventure show. The art style is kind of cool: it's very 70s/80s American cartoon style, but not quite. I'm not sure if I will keep watching it, but I think it's potentially actually a decent show.

So this one is definitely what I would call, at this point, a classic 90s shoujo isekai: girl has premonitions and gets mysteriously transported to another world. And it's animated by Studio Deen. Production quality isn't great, but the soundtrack is good. I haven't really gotten into the hook of it, but it's also not a show that I'm crazy about, so I'm not gonna continue further.

reviewed.titleEN: Even Though I'm a Super Timid Noble Girl, I Accepted the Bet From My Cunning Fiancé
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: So right off the bat this title is awful, but even more than that, I'm trying to figure out how many different fonts and accent styles they put in the actual title. I think it was at least five, but that's easy to do when you have a 16-word title. Meanwhile, apparently the show is going. I have no idea what it's really about, and I don't care, other than a sick girl who seems like she's been reverse-isekai'd from Tokyo to some sort of noble world, and now there's a knife-wielding person and she gets stabbed. But it's still just a dream. Oh good, now we're in another otome game isekai with an excessive amount of exposition.

reviewed.titleEN: Shinja Zero no Megami-sama to Hajimeru Isekai Kouryaku
reviewed.review: This one already looks terrible, and everybody wants to feel super cool, so they refused to play their opening before the show because they have no confidence in their opening. It's stupid, but it does have one slightly interesting thing: rather than just one person being isekai'd by a truck, I guess it's a whole train full of people who all froze to death and got sucked into another fantasy world. So it's kind of funny that everyone in the whole world is basically in on the whole isekai joke, even the people there, and they make fun of the main guy for his stats being low. If I were to watch a trash isekai show, I might go for this one, but it's probably gonna be pretty awful.

Surprisingly fun and good. It's 13 years after a zombie apocalypse, and that's all I know at this point, other than that the main characters left their isolated village for some reason. The art and production seem pretty decent. I like the character designs, I like the zombie designs, and the little pre-opening thing was short and simple enough that it worked without getting crazy exposition or super "we're such a cool show" vibes. And then the opening was pretty fun, so this could actually be a fairly fun, low-effort show.

So this appears to be some sort of Voltron-ish, space-invader kind of show. It could be OK, but here are the things that are kind of funny. The main guy is 13 years old, which is pretty young to be the lead of a show where you're leading a team of five, and the other four are all teenage girls, including at least one who is his older sister, who is 16. I think the interesting part is the five robots. I don't know whether they combine or not, but four of the pilots are cute high school girls and one is a guy, whereas if you go back previously, into straight-up sentai stuff, it's definitely the other way around: four guys and one girl. So that's kind of an interesting thing to think about here. They did a good, quick, very short expositional setup, which I don't mind as a pre-intro thing if it's 30 seconds long and then you play the intro. I've seen a couple of shows this season do that and I don't hate it at all. It's way better than a first episode that then runs for 10 minutes of exposition. Am I going to keep watching the show? Probably not, but it's not the worst thing I've seen, at least not at this point.

So this is a decent high fantasy, after-defeating-the-demon-army kind of show, and at least for the first part the production is pretty solid. The main character is a noble's daughter who is part of the hero's party and was engaged to him, but it seems like for whatever reason she didn't do anything in their battles. She was there, though, and then they called off the engagement. So it's all those things, but at least for the first part it's done well enough that I'm kind of curious. I don't think it's going to be anything fabulous, but it could be an entertaining show depending on which way it goes. I will say I really didn't think that highly of the opening. It just felt a little bland for my taste.

So this seems like a very Shonen Jump-style show, more like a team of five people with some sort of common special ability battling against others. In this case the special ability in this world is masks that are made and seem to imbue special powers into the wearers, and the main guy wants to destroy a certain mask because it killed a bunch of people when he was a kid. It seems like it should be totally fine if you want to watch that sort of show. The production seems all right, and from the opening and whatever else, the characters seem like a reasonable mix of spunky youth who want to defy authority and will certainly do battle with other mask users and non-mask users.

reviewed.titleEN: A Tale of the Secret Saint
reviewed.review: It's a high fantasy show. It seems fine, and the production doesn't seem bad. It's nothing that I'm losing my mind over, but I've definitely seen worse shows. So if you want a high fantasy with a female heroine who becomes a cleric/Saint rather than a knight but still wants to be a knight, or something like that, then this might be a show you'd watch.

I wasn't quite sure about this one from the title and the little synopsis, but watching the opening and the first bit of the show, it actually looks like it could be pretty interesting. It looks to be some sort of samurai-ish, maybe early Meiji kind of thing, or something like that. I can't quite tell yet. The production is nice. The opening was kind of cool and gave some good vibes for what the show is without just being a bunch of cut scenes from the show. The interaction between the first two sisters was actually kind of interesting, so I'm hopeful. It could actually be an interesting show. I'm not sure where it's going, but maybe it's good.

I never got into A Certain... when they first came out, and watching this year, the production value is quite nice. I recognize some of the characters from other stuff, but I just feel like I'm tossed into chapter 6 of some continuing story and I don't really know the others. It looks nice, so if someone convinces me that it's worth coming back to, I might do that. Otherwise I'm just going to skip it and watch something else.

It started out as some sort of crazy, weird robot spirit battle, and then it jumped back to the Bakumatsu period, old Edo. The production is pretty good throughout, with lots of really nice little bits. And then they throw in the twist, which is that this whole show is about a TCG that I guess existed back then, with all of the modern TCG trappings, fancy Yu-Gi-Oh!-looking printing and all the other crazy stuff. I was not expecting that, and I'll give it that. Am I going to keep watching? No, definitely not, but the production value is nice.

reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Well, that got really dark. It's about a teenage girl who gets involved in the world of foreign exchange stock market stuff, and it had the largest disclaimer I've ever seen in front of a show. It's pretty dark: it starts out at the financial collapse in 2008 and her mom trying to do some FX stuff and failing. But the opening is a crazy high-energy thing with four girls who I guess are all day traders but are also trying to be superheroes or something. I don't know. It's a little too intense for me.

Based on the title, I assume this is from some sort of game or something else. If it's "the animation," it's usually based off of a game of some sort, so this could potentially be cool. I have no idea what it's from, though; they could just like to call it the animation. It seems to be some sort of post-apocalyptic world, but there's still stuff like video games and things. I'm a bit intrigued by it. I really like the song for the opening, and the animation for the opening is nicely done. I'm not sure if I love it or not, but it's not bad, and the rest of the production looks pretty good. I like the soundtrack and I'm kind of curious about where the world's going to go, so it could be OK. It could be trash. Maybe I'll find out.

reviewed.titleEN: So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin?
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review:
You know, this makes me wonder how many vehicular deaths occur in Tokyo on an annual basis. Because if I'm to believe all of these shows, it's gotta be tens or hundreds of thousands of people killed every year by vehicles in just Tokyo. But I kind of doubt that. It's not like Japan is the USA, where we just kill hundreds of thousands of people every year in our murder machines.
Anyway, this is a show, and people have apparently produced it and made it and it's there. I don't really have any interest in this show at all. It looks pretty dumb.

reviewed.titleEN: The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life
reviewed.review:
So I think all this stuff with people getting kicked out of guilds, in the fantasy shows of which there are at least 10 this season, is really a reflection of people being fired or downsized from their jobs. In a way it can be empowering, because it says, oh well, you can be fired from your job, but then after 12 or 24 episodes you're super powerful and they regret ever letting you go. Plus there's the whole thing where people kick someone out, like in this show. I guess the guy is some sort of enchanter who doesn't fight, and they say, oh, we've enchanted everything so we don't need you anymore. That just feels pretty shortsighted, because someone who's good at their job and can do these things could clearly go and figure out something else that's useful to do. But I guess that's the modern world, particularly in these fantasy settings where you have literally the one thing you can do because that's your skill or your trade. And then these people are forced to figure out something else they can do, or some other way to use it.
OK, so now for the show review. The premise is kind of a standard skill-point-based, presumably high fantasy adventure show. It doesn't appear to be an isekai or video game show. I would say it's not a great premise, but P.A. Works has done a great job on the execution, at least for this first episode. It's got some really cool cuts, very interesting art changes and colors, and some actually pretty funny little bits in there. It's going to be a dumb show, which is fine if it's executed well, and hopefully the execution keeps up and it's a fun show to watch when I want something stupid done.

I ended up watching this whole episode just because it was on in the background while I was having dinner. It's another stupid skill-based thing, where the main character gets access to the Internet as her super skill, and it's literally the Internet. It happens that the world she's in is also some sort of game, so there are game facts on there with all sorts of detailed stuff, and she's able to get some super endgame equipment immediately. It's a dumb thing, which is fine. I guess my problem is that it's so hyper-focused on "oh, isn't she cute doing all the cute things that are cute" that it's just so over the top. It's not the worst thing I've ever seen, but it is offensively bland.

I didn't watch this one myself; a trusted friend whose opinion I pretty much agree with did, and here's his take: "Deciding that I need to suffer more, I watched ep 1 of MKR 2026. If you're going to reboot something 32 years later MAKE IT LOOK BETTER THAN THE ORIGINAL. Holy shit is it the most meh animation and art ever. I don't like Clamp anime, but I sure respect the art quality of MKR 94 way more than this trashcan."

reviewed.titleEN: The Cold Satou-san Is Only Sweet to Me
reviewed.review: So this is a show that someone decided needed to be made and animated and all these things, I guess. I mean, production is fine. The opening makes me kind of motion sick and the rest of it is just dumb stuff, so that's where I'm at for the show.
